reviewer: Codex implementation/source review; not independent security certification
scope_review: The surplus-Initial failure discovered during Q00 review is fixed by per-message input leasing and rejection of queued old-level surplus before events/readiness. The same external production probe now rejects with UnexpectedLevel; both roles and native budgets 1/16384 are covered by the tenth conformance test. Unchanged core, ABI and records evidence is reused after reviewing its unchanged execution closure; the actual Engine and production consumer are re-executed in both modes. The implemented native provider is Windows x86_64 with the exact OpenSSL 3.5.8 SDK and pinned Zig. LP64/other native targets explicitly remain unavailable, with no cross-build substituted for runtime/ABI evidence. T07/T09/T13 and the QUIC endpoint/resource/independent-interop graph remain unfinished. The direct reference adapter uses the same OpenSSL provider, bypasses the new C adapter/Engine and independently encrypts a genuine QUIC short-header packet; it is not independent QUIC endpoint interoperability. Existing records sources, package pins, frozen QUIC fixture and all SDK files are preserved. Production independently authored Zig extern declarations are the ABI under test, not a parallel test-only layout.

environment.powershell: pwsh from bundled Codex runtime; actual executable path resolved by shutil.which in test harness

overrides_native_runs.PATH: Python directory; pinned Zig directory; locked SDK bin; inherited PATH

environment.scope: Native Windows x86_64 only. Pure consumers cross-compile for seven additional targets; other native providers remain unavailable/unqualified.

acceptance.observed: Native LLP64 compares every size/alignment/member offset in five C/Zig types and C invokes all Zig callbacks with known fixed-width/struct arguments. Calls actual linked query symbol. Unsupported native targets are explicitly unavailable; no LP64 execution is claimed.

C invalid pointer/length, unknown level/direction, safe still-allocated closed handles and zero budgets preserve outputs/allocation ownership as specified. No invented/freed pointer is dereferenced; output owners are never overwritten.
